working_tree: Uncommitted implementation with previous review fixes; production code unchanged during this audit.
limitations: Small, deliberately selected route samples; not a random sample or whole-city validation.
Source snapshot replay exercises public loaders with the HTTP result replaced by cached real responses.
Tokyo, Sydney and Hong Kong used OSM API 0.6 because global Overpass requests timed out; way geometry was expanded from node references and route masters were not fetched.
Explicit repairs use PTv2 ordered stop members and point positions, with labelled audit placeholders for missing names; they do not validate a real timetable.
Reference GTFS archives are from 2025; exact reconstruction checks software fidelity, not present-day service validity.
Default speeds and empirical service accuracy were not calibrated or validated.
Full pytest was not rerun in this implementation audit; the previous implementation check had 1289 passing tests.

findings.title: Loaded GTFS stop tables cannot be reused without dropping their binary geometry column
findings.expected: A pandas stop table with valid stop_lat/stop_lon remains usable after load_gtfs; binary geometry is decoded or ignored consistently.
findings.actual: ValueError: geometry: supply a non-empty Point. load_gtfs exposes WKB in a pandas table; preflight assumes every geometry value is a Shapely object.
findings.workaround: Drop geometry when reusing the coordinate-valued pandas stop table.
findings.control: reuse_without_geometry_control passes; first observed with loaded MTA shuttle data.

findings.title: Automatic trip IDs collide with explicit IDs in partial service overrides
findings.expected: Retain the explicit ID and allocate a different unused ID to the completed pattern.
findings.actual: Explicit p0 trip_id=service_1 collides with the automatic ID for unlisted p1, causing ValueError.
findings.workaround: Avoid generated service_<number> IDs or supply all trip IDs explicitly.
findings.control: An explicit ID of explicit_trip passes with the same patterns.

findings.title: Valid numeric direction codes are rejected after passing preflight
findings.expected: Integral numerical codes 0.0 and 1.0 behave like 0 and 1, consistently with numeric preflight and output normalisation.
findings.actual: Later validation compares strings with 0/1 and rejects 0.0/1.0.
findings.workaround: Convert direction_id to integer or nullable Int64.
findings.control: Identical input with integer direction_id passes.

findings.title: Infinite route_type leaks OverflowError instead of a contextual input error
findings.expected: ValueError identifying routes, row and route_type.
findings.actual: int(infinity) raises OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer.
findings.workaround: Reject non-finite route_type values in caller validation.
